questions.text: The Chapman-Kolmogorov equation P^(m+n)_{ij} = Σ_k P^(m)_{ik} · P^(n)_{kj} says:
options: The chain must visit state k exactly once between steps m and n
The (m+n)-step probability from i to j equals the sum over all relay states k of the m-step probability from i to k times the n-step probability from k to j
The transition probabilities multiply by m+n
The chain can only make transitions at multiples of m and n
questions.explanation: The C-K equation decomposes a long journey (m+n steps from i to j) by conditioning on the state k visited at the midpoint (step m). You sum over all possible relay states k, multiplying the m-step probability of reaching k by the n-step probability of going from k to j.

questions.text: The stationary distribution π satisfies π P = π, meaning it is a left eigenvector of the TPM P with eigenvalue 1.
questions.explanation: The equation πP = π written as a row vector × matrix equation is equivalent to P^T π^T = π^T (eigenvalue equation with eigenvalue 1 for P^T). So π is a left eigenvector of P (or equivalently, a right eigenvector of P^T) with eigenvalue 1.

questions.text: If the stationary probability π_H = 0.60 for the Healthy state, what is the mean return time to the Healthy state?
questions.explanation: The ergodic theorem states π_i = 1 / E[return time to i]. Therefore E[return time to H] = 1/π_H = 1/0.60 ≈ 1.67 steps. If observations are weekly, a patient returns to the Healthy state on average every 1.67 weeks.

questions.text: In the proof of Chapman-Kolmogorov, which property is used to drop the condition X_0=i from P(X_{m+n}=j | X_m=k, X_0=i)?
options: The Markov property (the future depends only on the present, not on the past)
questions.explanation: Step 4 of the proof uses the Markov property: P(X_{m+n}=j | X_m=k, X_0=i) = P(X_{m+n}=j | X_m=k). Given the current state X_m=k, the earlier history X_0=i is irrelevant for the future.

questions.text: As n → ∞, the rows of P^n for an ergodic (irreducible, aperiodic, positive-recurrent) Markov chain:
options: All converge to the zero vector
All converge to the same vector π (the stationary distribution), regardless of starting row
questions.explanation: For an ergodic chain, the rows of P^n converge to π as n → ∞. This means that regardless of where the chain started (which row / starting state), after enough steps the distribution over states approaches the unique stationary distribution π.

questions.text: The Chapman-Kolmogorov equations imply that the n-step transition matrix is P^n (the n-th matrix power of the one-step TPM P).
questions.explanation: Setting m=1 in C-K gives P^(1+n) = P^1 × P^n = P × P^n. By induction from P^1 = P: P^2 = P×P, P^3 = P²×P, ..., P^n = P×P×...×P (n times). So P^(n) = P^n as a matrix power.
